My name is not important, but I am a woman of 55 years from the South East. This small piece behind my compound, only about half a plot, I use for yam and cassava together with some cocoyam and vegetables between the mounds. The land is my husband's family land so we do not pay for it, and I have been farming it many years. Money is tight so I will only buy a small bag of NPK to share across my plots, but I rely more on the droppings from my goats and the ash from the kitchen. For yam I keep my own seed yams from last harvest, but the cassava stems I collected some improved ones from the ADP extension officer last year that give better roots.
